title: Conformance case query
description: One query.json under conformance/testdata/cases/<name>/. Mirrors nosqlite.Query (query.go) plus a `dataset` name to look up in testdata/datasets/.

description.description: Optional prose: what behaviour this case pins down, when the case name alone does not carry it. Ignored by every runner.

dataset.description: Name of a file in testdata/datasets/ (without .json) to insert before running this query.

mutations.description: Writes applied after the dataset is seeded and before the query runs, in order. Omit for a read-only case. This is what lets a case cover write behaviour — the query below then observes the result.

op.description: Which write to perform. `insert` adds `document`. `replace` overwrites the first document matching `filter` with `document` in full. `delete` removes the first document matching `filter`; `delete_many` removes every match.

filter.description: Which document(s) to write to, for `replace`, `delete` and `delete_many`. Same Mongo-dialect grammar as the query `filter` below. Unused by `insert`. An empty filter on `delete_many` empties the collection.

document.description: Required for `insert` and `replace`, unused by the deletes. For `replace` it is the complete replacement document, not a diff — omitted fields are gone afterwards, and `_id` is immutable so include it only if it equals the matched document's. For `insert`, a supplied `_id` must be free: re-using a live one is an error, but an `_id` freed by an earlier `delete` is not.

matched.description: Optional assertion: the count the operation must return — 0 or 1 for `replace` and `delete`, any count for `delete_many`, and 1 for a successful `insert`. The runner checks it before running the query, so a case that mutates nothing fails here rather than confusingly further down. Mutually exclusive with `error` — a failed operation returns no count.

error.description: Optional assertion: the operation must fail, and the message must CONTAIN this text. A substring, not the whole message, because only the text is shared across the three bindings — Go returns an error, Python raises NoSQLiteError, TypeScript throws. The query below then runs against the unchanged data, which is how a case proves a rejected write wrote nothing.

filter.description: Mongo-dialect filter document (query.go's Query.Filter). A bare `"field": value` means equality. Operators — usable as a field's value, or $and/$or/$not at any level: $and, $or, $not, $eq, $ne, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in, $nin, $exists. Full grammar: docs/matcher.md.

projection.description: Which fields the query returns (query.go's Query.Projection). Keys are field paths; a value of 1 (or true) INCLUDES that field, 0 (or false) EXCLUDES it, and nothing else is accepted. `{"name": 1, "address.city": 1}` keeps only those fields; `{"email": 0}` keeps everything else. Inclusion and exclusion cannot be mixed in one projection, except `_id`, which is returned unless excluded with `{"_id": 0}`. A dotted key rebuilds the subdocument rather than flattening the key. Omit to return whole documents. A case using this normally sets `docs` in expected.json (without `fields`) so the projected shape itself is what gets compared.

sort.description: Sort keys applied in order. Omit for insertion order.

skip.description: Drop this many matches before returning any. Default 0.

limit.description: Cap the number of results returned. 0 or omitted means no limit.
